title: Curative Petition before the Supreme Court (Article 137 + Order XLVIII SC Rules, 2013)
description: Curative petition — the final remedy after dismissal of review petition, invoking the inherent jurisdiction of the Supreme Court to prevent abuse of its process and miscarriage of justice, on the narrow grounds laid down in Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra.

respondent_name.label: Respondent Name (as in original SC judgment)

original_judgment_date.label: Date of Original SC Final Judgment

options: Violation of principles of natural justice — petitioner not heard / not party served
Apprehension of bias — judge did not disclose connection
Manifest injustice / question of general public importance
curative_ground.label: Curative Ground (Rupa Ashok Hurra)

abuse_specifics.label: Particulars of abuse of process / manifest injustice

open_court_hearing_sought.label: Pray for open court hearing (default is chambers circulation)

relief_sought.label: Relief — recall/modification of impugned final judgment

mandatory_clauses: Cause title in form 'Curative Petition (Civil/Criminal) No. ___ of ___ In Review Petition (Civil/Criminal) No. ___ of ___ In [Original case]'
Invocation of Article 137 of Constitution + Order XLVIII of SC Rules, 2013
Recital of original judgment — date, bench, citation, holding
Recital of review petition — filing, hearing mode, dismissal date
Specific ground from Rupa Ashok Hurra grounds — not merely a re-argument
Statement that grounds were either raised in review OR not available at review stage with reasons
Senior advocate's certificate certifying that curative grounds exist (mandatory — Order XLVIII Rule 2(2))
Prayer for circulation before the bench that passed final judgment + senior-most three judges of SC
If open court sought: separate prayer with reasons

prompt_context.system_role: You are drafting a Curative Petition under Article 137 of the Constitution read with Order XLVIII of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013. This is the final remedy after dismissal of a review petition. Cite Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra (2002) 4 SCC 388 — the curative jurisdiction was crafted to prevent (a) violation of principles of natural justice where the petitioner was not heard or not served, (b) apprehension of bias from a judge who did not disclose connection, (c) abuse of process of the court, (d) manifest injustice. Grounds must be those NOT taken at review or, if taken, not addressed. A curative petition is NOT a second review. It is heard in chambers in circulation by the three senior-most judges and the judges who passed the impugned judgment (if available), and is dismissed without hearing unless the bench is prima facie satisfied. Order XLVIII Rule 2(2) mandates a senior advocate's certificate certifying the grounds.
prompt_context.tone: extreme deference to the Court; restrained; non-repetitive of review grounds
style_notes: Do NOT re-argue the merits of the original case — that is impermissible
Explicitly state which Rupa Ashok Hurra ground is invoked
Explicitly state whether the ground was urged in review or was unavailable then
Frame prayer modestly — for recall, reconsideration, or such other relief as the Court deems fit
Senior advocate's certificate must be a separate document filed with the petition

relevantActs.notes: Article 137 — review jurisdiction; curative is a derivative inherent jurisdiction
Order XLVIII Rules 1-4 govern curative petitions; Rule 2(2) requires senior advocate certificate

key_precedents.case: Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra
key_precedents.principle: Foundational — curative jurisdiction recognised; grounds limited to NJP, judge bias non-disclosure, abuse of process, manifest injustice

key_precedents.case: Sumer v. State of Uttar Pradesh
key_precedents.principle: Curative petition is exception, not rule — confined to narrow grounds

key_precedents.case: Yakub Abdul Razak Memon v. State of Maharashtra
key_precedents.principle: Curative in capital cases — procedure when death warrant issued

key_precedents.case: National Commission for Women v. State of Delhi
key_precedents.principle: Curative may be heard in open court in exceptional circumstances

filing_checklist: Curative petition with proper cause title
Senior advocate's certificate (Order XLVIII Rule 2(2)) — separately signed
Certified copy of original SC judgment
Certified copy of order dismissing review petition
Affidavit of petitioner sworn before Oath Commissioner
Statement in petition that grounds were taken at review or were unavailable
Filed only through AOR — direct filing not permitted
Note on prayer for open court hearing if sought

validation_rules.rule: review_dismissal_date must exist and be prior to filing (curative not maintainable until review is dismissed)
At least one curative_ground from Rupa Ashok Hurra grounds must be selected
senior_advocate_name must be filled — certificate is mandatory under Order XLVIII Rule 2(2)
aor_name must be filled — curative filed only through AOR
Petition must not be a re-argument of review grounds — flag if pleading reads like merits re-argument
If NJP ground invoked, natural_justice_specifics must be filled
If bias ground invoked, bias_specifics must be filled

procedure_notes.default_hearing_mode: Chambers — circulation among three senior-most judges + judges who passed final judgment, if available
procedure_notes.open_court: Heard in open court only if the bench so directs after preliminary view
procedure_notes.dismissal_pattern: Vast majority dismissed at threshold without reasons; success rate extremely low — to be set out honestly to client
procedure_notes.limitation: No specific limitation; must be filed within reasonable time after review dismissal — explain any delay
